records.confusion: Candidates predicted oxygen at a copper anode as though the electrode were inert; the report explains that the copper electrode takes part in the reaction.
records.diagnostic_test: Compare the anode product for copper(II) sulfate using a copper anode and an inert carbon anode; explain the role of the electrode.

records.confusion: Candidates treated preparation of an insoluble salt as though it required evaporation and crystallisation.
records.diagnostic_test: Choose the separation steps for an insoluble precipitate and a soluble salt made in solution, explaining why the sequences differ.

records.confusion: Candidates confused reaction rate with the time taken by a reaction.
records.diagnostic_test: Given two reaction curves, identify which is faster using gradient rather than total elapsed time.

records.confusion: Some candidates added burette readings or subtracted them in the wrong order instead of finding the titre.
records.diagnostic_test: Calculate a titre from two burette readings, stating which reading is initial and which is final.

records.confusion: Candidates confused atoms and elements and did not consistently use proton and neutron numbers to identify isotopes.
records.diagnostic_test: Given proton, neutron and electron counts, select isotopes of one element and explain the shared and differing counts.

records.confusion: Candidates mixed up flame tests with gas tests involving a lighted or glowing splint.
records.diagnostic_test: Match a flame colour test, a glowing splint test and a lighted splint test to the substances each can identify.

records.confusion: Candidates confused an isotope with an allotrope.
records.diagnostic_test: Decide whether two carbon structures are isotopes or allotropes, and justify using atomic nuclei versus structure.

records.confusion: Candidates did not distinguish a mole from the Avogadro constant.
records.diagnostic_test: Distinguish one mole as an amount of substance from the Avogadro constant as particles per mole.

records.confusion: Candidates confused tests using a glowing splint and a lighted splint.
records.diagnostic_test: Choose the correct splint test for oxygen and hydrogen, then state the expected result of each.

records.confusion: Candidates named electrons rather than mobile ions as charge carriers in a molten ionic compound.
records.diagnostic_test: Explain conductivity in molten magnesium chloride by naming the moving charged particles; contrast these with electrons in a metal.

records.confusion: Candidates added masses at different times instead of subtracting them to find mass lost during an interval.
records.diagnostic_test: Given two mass readings at different times, calculate the mass lost over that interval and explain the subtraction.

records.confusion: Candidates described green copper(II) carbonate as blue, apparently confusing the solid with copper(II) sulfate.
records.diagnostic_test: Compare the appearance of copper(II) carbonate powder with blue copper(II) sulfate solution.

records.confusion: A flat gas-volume curve was described as equilibrium or a constant reaction rather than a completed reaction.
records.diagnostic_test: Explain what a plateau in a gas-volume-versus-time graph means for reactant consumption and rate.

records.confusion: Some plans treated the marked-cross paper as chromatography paper rather than placing it beneath the flask to time clouding.
records.diagnostic_test: Place a marked cross in a disappearing-cross rate experiment and explain how it signals the endpoint.

records.confusion: Candidates counted bromide-ion electrons as though bromide were a neutral bromine atom.
records.diagnostic_test: Count electrons in bromine and bromide, then explain the one-electron difference from charge.

records.confusion: Some candidates drew covalent sharing instead of electron transfer when representing magnesium bromide.
records.diagnostic_test: Draw electron transfer for magnesium bromide and distinguish it from a covalent shared pair.

records.confusion: Some candidates used the word electrons instead of ions in their answers to Q2(d)(ii).
records.diagnostic_test: Name the charge carrier in molten magnesium bromide and explain why it can move.

records.confusion: Some candidates did not distinguish an atom from an ion when explaining electron and proton counts.
records.diagnostic_test: Given proton and electron counts, classify a particle as an atom or an ion and state the reason.

records.confusion: Candidates called the deep-blue solution after excess ammonia a precipitate, losing the distinction between solid and dissolved product.
records.diagnostic_test: After excess ammonia is added to a copper(II) mixture, distinguish the precipitate from the coloured solution.
